findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A review finds a blocking issue while the parent’s CI is running. `after_code_ci` still returns when `serious` is set (`src/forge/checks.py:138`), and close then pushes the record (`src/forge/close.py:430`). The workflow cancels the parent (`src/forge/prcheck.py:52`), leaving no completed successful run for reuse (`src/forge/templates/review-tests.py:125`), so the record starts the full suite. This case was raised in the previous round and remains; excluding it would require the owner to narrow the Done-when to clean-review pushes.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - Close saves a review while the code’s CI is running. The revised test supplies running-then-green check responses and asserts two lookups, but never runs the record head’s workflow or verifies that its suite is skipped. It would still pass if reuse always returned false. The separate reuse test starts with a completed parent and creates its record independently of close (`tests/test_review_record_reuses_parent_tests.py:89` and `tests/test_review_record_reuses_parent_tests.py:123`), so it does not cover the requested transition.
findings.title: Gate: prove the running parent finishes and its result is reused

why: Issue 1656: in CI-test repos, close pushes its review record commit a few minutes after the code, and that push cancels the code's own CI run in progress (concurrency cancel-in-progress). The parent then has no successful run, so .forge/review-tests.py cannot reuse it, and every record-only commit starts a full run again: 72% of one client's runs, about 28 minutes each.
